To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the dispersion of Bloch modes in the structure of alternating LHM and RHM can be described in terms of the effective permittivity and effective permeability of the LHM-RHM composite; (2) the effective parameters of the composite are complex-valued; (3) the dispersion of the Bloch modes can be described in the framework of a simple effective-medium theory (EMT), and (4) the EMT is in excellent agreement with rigorous numerical calculations.
(a) there are no pass bands for the TM-polarization, (b) there are pass bands for the TE-polarization, and (c) the pass bands of the TE-polarizaton are not necessarily overlapping.

(1) the periodic multilayers with alternating left-handed (LH) and right-handed materials (RH) can support both TEand TM-guided eigenmodes; (2) the frequency pass bands of both polarizations may overlap, thus allowing for an efficient radiation energy transfer across the multilayer; and (3) the dispersion properties are determined not only by the Bloch wave number, but also by the surface wave number.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of Bloch modes in a one-dimensional periodic structure with alternating right-handed and left-handed materials.
a study of the dispersion of Bloch modes of a multilayer structure composed of alternating layers of left-handed and right- handed materials.
the dispersion properties of Bloch modes of a periodic structure with alternating right-handed and left-handed materials.

, in the case of the left-handed material, the pass bands for the TM-polarized waves are always wider than for TE-polarized waves.
the dispersion properties of the Bloch modes in a periodic multilayer with alternating left-handed (LHM) and right-handed materials (RHM) are very rich and complex.

the multilayer structure under study supports a variety of different types of eigenmodes, including both left-handed and right- handed modes, which are characterized by different dispersion properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a periodic multilayer composed of alternating left-handed and ordinary right-handed materials can support guided modes with both TE and TM polarizations.
a multilayer structure with alternating left- and right-handed materials can be a promising candidate to design a novel optical device with unique dispersion properties.
the dispersion properties of the Bloch modes are determined by the effective refractive index of the multilayer structure and by the effective permittivity of the constituent materials.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of a pass band for one polarization does not necessarily guarantee a pass band for the other polarization.
the multilayer structure with alternating LHM and RHM can support all-evanescent modes, which are localized in the vicinity of the surface and propagate in the direction perpendicular to the surface.

Bloch modes in a periodic multilayer can be excited in a wide frequency band and, depending on the frequency, the Bloch wave number kB, and the surface wave number kS, can have different properties, such as being leaky or non-leaky, propagating, evanescent, and/or guided.
